Copied: paste it into the page, then submit there

With both the endpoint URL and the model id filled in, video mode sends that turn to this model (an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and it shows up in dsh\'s own model list as "Luwi 视频模式"); one of the two alone is not enough and the model above stays in use. The API key is stored in this configuration and only its masked form is shown - clear the URL to go back to the model above
Endpoint URL: an http(s) address, usually with /v1, such as https://api.deepseek.com/v1
API key: the key this endpoint accepts; leave it blank when your own gateway needs none
Model id: the id the endpoint accepts, such as deepseek-chat
Back to the model above (the API key is kept, so filling this in again needs no retyping)
How far a picture is shrunk before the model sees it
Screenshot what is being pointed at
When a line says "this", "this picture", "on the screen" or "in the photo", attach a picture of the phone\'s own screen to it before it is sent (never in video mode)
Scale a screenshot to this many pixels before the model sees it
Shrink a PNG further while it is over %1$d bytes, which is the ceiling this app sets; the route has its own limit in settings.yaml (imageMaxBytes), and a picture over that fails the model request
In KiB, and typing goes up to %2$d; a value over the slider top %1$d needs imageMaxBytes raised in settings.yaml first
Which model speaks in video mode, how many frames, how far apart
Nobody is holding the camera: looking and switching to video mode are not blocked
Session %1$s has held the camera since %2$s; tap this row to release it
%1$d ms between one frame and the next; one capture costs a couple of hundred milliseconds on its own, so this is what it asks for, not what it gets
%1$d frame(s) each time the camera is asked to look; the agent can name another number for one call, and this is the default it starts from
Capture at up to %1$d pixels; it takes effect the next time the camera opens, and the app reopens it right away when it is already running

Lay the frames out as one picture as well; the agent reads that one first, so a dozen frames cost one look instead of twelve. Each cell is a smaller copy, so it is for seeing what moved, not for reading small text

These are the app\'s half of the video mode camera: how many frames, how far apart, how big, and whether they also come back as one grid. The route has its own budgets in settings.yaml (imagePixelBudget, imageMaxBytes), and a picture over those is re-encoded on the host before the model sees it
%1$s s; a shorter value sends the sentence sooner, but a normal pause can get cut into two sentences
Say the word and it listens
Listening for %1$s; a hit or a tap on the ball listens for one sentence
Listening for %1$s, and the resident chain is running too (what video mode asks for: it keeps listening after a sentence)
Allowed to wake, but the service is not running; turn the switch off and on again
Not listening; the switch below starts it
The microphone permission is not granted yet; the Permissions section below has the entry
Model ready: %1$d files, each checked against its sha256
Not downloaded yet, about %1$s in all
%1$d of %2$d files are in place; tap to fetch the rest
Nothing set yet; the default %1$s is what is being watched for (tap to change it)

One word per line, written as word=pinyin with tone numbers, for example 肥鱼肥鱼=fei2 yu2 fei2 yu2. The pinyin becomes the symbols the model knows, and anything missing from its table is refused instead of dropped quietly
Let this app listen for the wake word (a local 3.3M keyword model, 5.3 MB). It is only permission: the microphone starts guarding that word once this is on, and the notification keeps a Stop button

Stops the wake word listener only: the microphone goes fully off, so calling the word does nothing. The host, the ball and the notification stay, and tapping the ball still listens for one sentence. This is a switch for right now; it does not touch the permission above
Power save is on: the microphone is closed and the wake word does nothing; tapping the ball still listens for one sentence (turn the switch below off to go back)
No schedule; tap to write one range, for example %1$s
Roughly %1$s; power save starts and ends on its own inside it
Inside that range right now (%1$s), so power save is in effect
One range, written like 23:00-07:00 (crossing midnight is fine). Clearing the line turns the schedule off
That does not read as a time range; write one like 23:00-07:00 (hours 0-23, minutes 0-59)
Identical start and end is an empty window, which would never save power; pick another time or clear the line to turn the schedule off
Power save also stops the automatic commands\' watches
Only the two expensive ones stop (weather and place); notifications, the foreground app, light and time carry on
The wake word model is not downloaded yet; the download row below is what gets it
What a hit does beyond buzzing, beeping and bringing the app forward. The two mode rows go through the same command path as saying it out loud, and that table lives on the host side in one place
Also switch back to phone mode
A 500 ms buzz when the word is heard; off leaves the short beep, and the app still comes forward
One ball, tap it to talk

On: a small ball stays over other apps - tap it to speak, hold it for a menu, drag it to an edge to tuck it away. It needs the display-over-other-apps permission, and a missing one is named instead of failing quietly
How long a press counts, how far a finger may drift, how quick a triple tap must be, how close two taps must be to count as a double tap, and how long two taps must be kept apart; now: %1$s
How big the ball is in dp (48-80); bigger is easier to see, smaller gets in the way less. Takes effect right away (the ball resizes within half a second); if it does not, restart Luwi. Now: %1$d dp
Your setting is %1$d dp, but the look you picked needs at least %2$d dp (its artwork is a full-body drawing), so it is %3$d dp right now. Takes effect right away; if it does not, restart Luwi
On: after five idle seconds the whole ball fades to 35% opacity, so it hides less of what is under it; touch it and it goes back to full. The breathing while speaking or listening is unchanged
On: after five idle seconds the ball slides half of itself off the screen edge; touch it and it comes back. Off: it stays fully out and only moves when you drag it
The ball is not on screen right now
The display-over-other-apps permission is missing, so the switch above will not put a ball up
The host has not reported a GUI address yet; the ball can talk, while the keyboard strip waits for that address

Move the ball up a little before dragging it sideways: while it hugs the left or right edge, dragging it straight inward crosses the system\'s back gesture first, which leaves the ball where it was and takes you out of the app instead
The ball did not come off, so it is still on screen: %1$s
There is no dsh GUI address yet, so the keyboard strip cannot open (try again once the host is up)
This device has no window manager, so no ball can be drawn

The host is not up yet, so this line is queued: it goes out once the host is running
The wake word model is not downloaded yet; use that row in the settings page
A reply is being spoken, so it is not listening
The interrupt did not go out: the voice inbox is not writable
On: every finished reply is spoken out loud. Off: nothing is spoken on its own, while asking for a line (lw_speak) and the Listen row below still work
Cut off what is being said right now
On: the rate set on the system\'s text-to-speech page is what you hear. Turning this off, or dragging the slider below, makes this app set its own
Following the system setting; drag this to choose one here
This voice is simply a quiet one; dragging up adds gain
What you hear above 100%% is gain; the ceiling is 300%%
In percent, from %1$d to %2$d; 100%% is this voice\'s own level
The system engine keeps its own volume and this app has no API for it: speaking with that engine follows the phone\'s media volume. The slider shows up with an imported voice
The engine has not come up yet; tap to try again

In use; pick a voice below
Speaks with a sherpa-onnx model from the voices directory; slower to start, but the voice is yours
Speaks through Microsoft Edge\'s read-aloud endpoint with no key; the voices are the ones it offers online
An endpoint-accepted voice name such as zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural; blank goes back to the default
A full handshake and one short sentence (collected, not played). It also says whether the local token or the token endpoint was used
Posts the text to an OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech endpoint and speaks with the voice that service gives
Fill in the address and key below
Not set yet: for example https://api.openai.com, or your own gateway
A domain, .../v1 or the full endpoint all work; /v1/audio/speech is appended when missing
Not set yet; leave it blank when your own gateway needs no key
Set (kept in this app\'s preferences only)
Sent as Bearer; kept in this app\'s preference file and never echoed back
A model name the endpoint accepts, such as tts-1; blank goes back to the default
A voice name the endpoint accepts, such as alloy; blank goes back to the default
This engine\'s loudness comes from the service and the phone\'s media volume; the gain here only applies to the imported model
Nothing found under %1$s; drop a model directory there and tap to scan again
%1$s model; tap to speak with it
%1$s\nOne directory per voice; tap to scan again
Where the engine itself, its voice packs and its own rate live; this app can only pick among the voices that engine offers
Says one line with the voice and rate above, so the choice can be judged by ear
This is how a reply will be spoken.
Waking the screen up, then walking through your own unlock
Light up the screen when the wake word is heard

The wake word is heard with the screen off too; without this, that hit lands in a dark room. The privileged channel is the first route (KEYCODE_WAKEUP), the app\'s own wake lock is the second, and a full-screen notification is the last one
Unlock the phone when the wake word is heard

Walks your own recorded unlock through, so a wake word reaches the home screen. This hands the unlock password to this app: fingerprints and faces cannot be replayed by an app, and a pattern is experimental. Off by default, every replay leaves a line in the notifications, and three failures in a row turn it off again
Inject the password instead of replaying the recording

Unlocking is faster with this on: the screen is lit, the password is typed in and confirmed, and no recorded gesture is replayed - the pauses between steps go away as well (measured on a real phone: with the screen on, the password alone unlocks it, with no gesture at all). Set the password under Inject password below; recording the unlock is not required first. If this phone\'s lock screen does not take injected input, or the unlock is a pattern, turn this off and use Record the unlock instead - the recording is always kept and this switch never deletes it. Three failures in a row turn off the unlock switch above
Not set yet; tap to enter the password or PIN used for injection, without recording an unlock first
%1$d characters saved; tap to change it, or save an empty one to clear it

Used by injection only: with the screen on, this password is typed in and confirmed. It is encrypted with a Keystore key, is never written into an unlock script and never appears in the logs; saving an empty value clears it. Use Try it once afterwards to check it
Nothing recorded yet; tap to walk your own unlock through once
%1$d step(s), in place since %2$s; the password slot holds %3$s
%1$d step(s), in place since %2$s; the password slot holds %3$s - injection is on, so turn it off and this recording is used instead if injection does not work here
Recording: walk through the unlock on the phone (%1$d step(s) so far)

Type the password or PIN here if this phone has one (leave it empty for a phone that only needs a swipe). Starting locks the screen; then walk through the unlock on the phone the way you always do, and it stops by itself once the phone is open. The taps that type a password are never written down: everything from the first tap on is dropped from the recording and this password is sent instead, encrypted with a Keystore key and never kept as plain text
Write the unlock out as a script instead of walking through it; the box starts from a template
%1$d step(s) are in place; open this to read them as a script, edit them and put them back

One step per line, and blank lines or anything after a # is ignored. The verbs are key, tap, swipe, stroke, text and wait - for example \"swipe 0.5 0.85 0.5 0.2 700\". Coordinates are 0 to 1 ratios of the screen rather than pixels, so 540 1200 is refused. text means \"a password is typed here\" and takes no argument: the password is never written into a script, it goes into the encrypted slot from the field below. This replaces whatever was recorded or imported before
Password / PIN, if the script has a text step
Locks the screen first, then runs one unlock with the current settings (with injection on, that is what gets tested) and reports how far it got
Deletes the steps, the plain copy of them in the workspace, the encrypted password and its Keystore key
the recording is gone, and the encrypted password went with its Keystore key
Nothing has been tried yet. The recording keeps only the moves: the password goes into the encrypted slot, and the taps that typed it are dropped on purpose
One read-only exploration a day; she rewrites the next task herself
It starts one by itself at that time; no tap needed
Once a day: write HH:mm (for example 03:00) and it starts by itself at that time
The time has to be HH:mm, for example 03:00
At most %1$d steps per run (1-1000, 60 by default)
The power-save probe could not be read this time, so it ran as if not in power save
No summary yet (the first run has not finished)

(empty: it will explore the phone freely)

She rewrites this card after every exploration (memory + what that run found); you can also edit it here
%1$d of %2$d said today; it skips once the limit is reached
For her to open a conversation on her own, turn on 允许它自己动手 in Automatic commands; a run skipped because the host was down is recorded here
When something happens, do something (say a line, or open a conversation to work)
No automatic commands yet. They live in %1$s; tap New below and say in one line when it should fire and what it should do, and the model writes the rule
Say in one line when and what; the model writes the conditions and the parameters

One line is enough: when it should fire and what it should do. You also pick the cooldown (0 to 1440 minutes, 0 means no cooldown); the model writes the rule as JSON, and it shows up on this page once it is written
For example: remind me to take an umbrella at eight every day
请把下面这件事做成一条自动指令, 用 lw_automation op=write 写进 automations, 名字你起一个短的中文名, when 挑最合适的那一种条件, then 用 remind (提醒一声) 或 task (开一场会话去干活); 冷却时间必须写成 cooldownMinutes: %2$d 分钟 —— 这是主人自己定的, 不许改成别的数: %1$s
Pick a rule first, then pick what to do with it
Then choose: run it once / change the cooldown / change it / delete it
Say in one line what to change; the model reads the rule as it is now and writes the new one back
For example: make it weekdays at eight, twice a day at most
请改一改自动指令「%1$s」: %2$s —— 先用 lw_automation op=read 读它现在是什么, 再用 op=write 把改好的写回去
Deletes the file "%1$s", with no way back
"%1$s" was not deleted: the file is gone or could not be removed
How long a rule waits before it may fire again: 0 to 1440 minutes, 0 means no cooldown. It takes effect at once
The cooldown was not changed: the rule cannot be read or the file is not writable
Handed over: every firing opens a conversation of its own, and the wording of a reminder is written then

The nine watches: nothing is registered while no enabled rule needs it (that is the low-power promise)
How often the weather is asked
The cheap, key-free source (Open-Meteo); one request per place, shared by every rule that needs it
How often the place is asked
Network location only (WiFi and cell), which almost never wakes the GPS; power save keeps the whole watch unregistered
How far the phone must move
Less than this is not "a different place"
Conditions are still judged in this window, they just stay silent (a different account from power save)
Write it as 23:00-07:00; crossing midnight works, and the same start and end means never quiet
That time could not be read, so nothing was changed
Let it act on its own
While this is on, the rules marked task really go and do it (off by default); reminders are not held back by it
Nothing has been decided yet. If a rule should have fired, the watch states above and the line about what is holding it back are the answer
The model writes the rules; this page only reads them. A rule\'s switch turns it on and off, and the other actions live under "Delete or change one"
The workflows that run from one tap, one Markdown file each

Say in one line what it should do; the model writes the body
One line is enough: what should this quick command do. The model picks the name and writes the steps, and it shows up on this page once it is written
For example: move this week\'s meetings to the morning
Run: hand it to the current conversation (a new one when there is none) and the model follows it. Delete: removes the file, with no way back
请把下面这件事做成一条快捷指令, 用 lw_quick op=write 写进 quick-commands, 名字你起一个短的中文名, 正文只写工作流 (先加载哪个技能, 再一步一步做什么): %1$s
Handed over: it joins the current conversation, opens one when there is none, or steers the turn already running

Removes the %1$s folder under the dsh home (there is no trash: anything you edited by hand is gone for good; "add" can only copy the bundled copy back)

Skills are plain prompt material: they land in the dsh home as SKILL.md files and change nothing about permissions. Editing one is expected - installing never overwrites an existing one; the installed page has check-for-updates, upgrade-all and remove, the available page has refresh, install-all and one-by-one install
Lists every skill in %1$s with its version: pick one to install, or upgrade an installed one
Search by name or what it does

Not a security sandbox: what runs inside cannot read this app\'s credentials (a different uid blocks that), but it buys shell-level reach, which is wider than the app itself; /work is the session workspace and nothing else is visible - and that is a proot-level convention, not a boundary; the network is open and cannot be closed. Each command is one-shot
Unpacks the bundled Alpine into /data/local/tmp/lwlinux, replacing the rootfs from scratch (packages installed inside are not coming back from anywhere but a fresh apk add)
Deletes the whole rootfs and everything apk add put into it

Deletes the whole rootfs under /data/local/tmp/lwlinux and every package installed into it - there is no trash, and reinstalling gets back only the bundled base. (With the channel down this directory is beyond even this button: adb is then the only way to clean it)

Off by default. Pair once with the QR code from the computer panel (repository, branch, peer address and token all arrive together), and sessions travel between the machines. The cross-device channel that lets the computer do the work lives here too - it is unrelated to sync and always available
